subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add editable workspace-wide and/or host-system file browsing to Control UI, and what permission boundary should replace the current allowlisted editor?
rationale: Current main intentionally separates the allowlisted editor from read-only workspace browsing; writes and host-system browsing would broaden what operator clients can read or mutate through Gateway.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only Mutations
options.body: Design bounded `agents.workspace.*` mutation methods with admin scopes, fs-safe containment, size limits, audit posture, and Control UI proof while keeping host-system browsing out of this issue.

options.title: Keep Read-Only Workspace Browsing
options.body: Preserve the current allowlisted editor plus read-only workspace preview until maintainers accept a stronger need for browser-based workspace writes.

options.title: Split System Files Into A New Design
options.body: Treat full host filesystem browsing as a separate high-risk design with explicit operator opt-in, read-only default, destructive-operation recovery, and security review.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only Mutations
recommendation.body: Design bounded `agents.workspace.*` mutation methods with admin scopes, fs-safe containment, size limits, audit posture, and Control UI proof while keeping host-system browsing out of this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the landed read-only workspace API and adjacent file-viewer fixes, making them the clearest owner for the remaining product/security boundary choice.
